lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: sequences as functions on the integers
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: sequences as functions on the integers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

steps: Input 1 appears twice with different outputs.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 105 components and consumes 2 per hour. It can run for at most 8 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 105 − 2h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = 3 and a(n) = a(n − 1) − 3 for n > 1. Find a(9).
In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time crosses the horizontal axis. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the y-intercept, giving the launch height
a zero, giving the time the projectile returns to ground level
the average rate of change over the flight
the maximum, giving the greatest height

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 7), (4, 9)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 140 components and consumes 12 per hour. It can run for at most 34 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 140 − 12h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = -10 and a(n) = a(n − 1) − 2 for n > 1. Find a(6).
In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time reaches its highest point. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the maximum, giving the greatest height and the time it occurs
the y-intercept, giving the launch height
the x-intercept, giving the landing time
an interval of decrease

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Does the relation x = y², for real y define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 95 components and consumes 4 per hour. It can run for at most 7 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 95 − 4h in this context?
choices: all real numbers
